candidates.primary_query: goed remmen met een scooter voorrem en achterrem
candidates.intent_rationale: Dutch-speaking travellers who rent a scooter in Vietnam often ride rarely at home and want to know how to brake safely with front and rear brakes, what combined braking and ABS do, and how to check the brakes before riding.
candidates.content_angle: Explains the Oregon DMV motorcycle manual's braking guidance (use both brakes every time; the front brake can provide 70 percent or more of stopping power; squeeze smoothly rather than grab; reduce lean before braking harder in a curve; integrated systems link both brakes) and what Honda Vietnam says about ABS on the LEAD ABS, plus how to test the brakes at pickup.
candidates.working_title: Goed remmen op een scooter: voorrem, achterrem en ABS

references.title: Oregon DMV, handboek voor motoren en bromfietsen, hoofdstuk 4: voertuigbeheersing (stoppen, gecombineerde remsystemen)

NL-S07 geeft tips voor scooterrijden in de regen in Hanoi. Dit onderwerp legt de remtechniek uit die je in elk weer nodig hebt, met de verdeling tussen voor- en achterrem.

candidates.primary_query: haarspeldbochten rijden met een scooter tips
candidates.intent_rationale: Dutch-speaking travellers heading to the northern mountain loops on a rented scooter want to know how to ride tight hairpin bends safely, what the dangerous-bend signs mean and what the law asks of riders on bends and passes.
candidates.content_angle: Explains the Oregon DMV four-step turning technique (slow before the curve, look through it, roll on the throttle, press the handgrip to lean), the dangerous-bend warning signs W.201 and W.202 in QCVN 41:2024/BGTVT with the regulation's definition of a dangerous bend in lowland and mountain areas, and the duty in Article 12(3)(c) and (d) of Law 36/2024/QH15 to slow down at bends, passes and slopes.
candidates.working_title: Haarspeldbochten op de scooter: zo rijd je veilig door bergbochten

candidates.primary_query: getuige van een verkeersongeluk in vietnam wat doen
entities: de plaats van het ongeluk beveiligen
candidates.intent_rationale: Dutch-speaking travellers on a scooter sometimes come across an accident they were not involved in and want to know what Vietnamese law expects from bystanders, how to help and whom to call.
candidates.content_angle: Explains the duties of people present at an accident under Article 80(2) of Law 36/2024/QH15 (help the injured, notify the police, a medical facility or the local People's Committee, help protect the scene and the victim's property, give information on request), Article 80(3) on using vehicles involved only when no other transport exists, Article 80(4) on passing drivers taking injured people to emergency care, Article 81(1) on reporting, and the emergency numbers 113, 114 and 115.

candidates.primary_query: hoeveel uur per dag scooter rijden vietnam
secondary_queries: voor het donker aankomen scooter vietnam
entities: pauze van 15 minuten na twee uur
candidates.intent_rationale: Dutch-speaking travellers planning a multi-day scooter trip in Vietnam want to know how many hours a day are realistic, how often to take breaks and how to recognise and avoid fatigue.
candidates.content_angle: Uses the UK Highway Code rule 91 recommendations (do not start a journey tired, take a break of at least 15 minutes after every two hours, stop somewhere safe when sleepy) and the duty in Article 12(2) of Law 36/2024/QH15 to adapt speed to road, terrain, traffic and weather to show how to plan realistic daily stages, breaks and arrival before dark, without inventing distance norms.

secondary_queries: scooter wegzetten en op de standaard zetten

candidates.content_angle: Builds a step-by-step practice plan for a quiet, empty area based on the UK compulsory basic training syllabus (element B: controls, stands, wheeling the machine; element C: moving off, slow control, braking, turning, U-turns, emergency stop) and applies it to the controls of a typical automatic rental scooter as described in Honda Vietnam's Vision owner's manual.

candidates.primary_query: elektrische scooter vietnam actieradius en opladen
secondary_queries: hoe ver rijdt een elektrische scooter vietnam
candidates.intent_rationale: Dutch-speaking travellers considering an electric rental scooter in Hanoi want to know how far it really goes, how long charging takes and how to charge it safely at a hotel or homestay.
candidates.content_angle: Uses VinFast's published Evo200 specifications (range measured at 30 km/h with one 65 kg rider and lower figures at higher speeds; charging times by charger type) to explain why real-world range is lower, and the fire police and Ministry of Public Security advice on safe charging (manufacturer charger, let the battery cool after riding, do not charge overnight or unattended, dry and ventilated place away from flammable material).
